newsitem.title: BOSNIA: 105 Moslem bodies unearthed in Bosnia - radio.
newsitem.headline: 105 Moslem bodies unearthed in Bosnia - radio.

text.p: Investigators said on Monday they had exhumed 105 bodies from two mass graves in northwestern Bosnia believed to contain Moslems killed by Serbs at the beginning of the war, state radio reported.

Bosnian investigators digging over the past week found 77 bodies at one site, which they believed to be those of men from the village of Velagici near the town of Kljuc, killed by advancing Bosnian Serb forces on June 1, 1992, the radio said.
Another 80 villagers are still missing, the radio said.
Investigators are still working on a second site, a cave where 28 bodies were unearthed on Monday.
They say the cave is believed to contain up to 150 bodies of civilians from the village of Biljani, also close to Kljuc.
Kljuc was controlled by Bosnian Serb forces for three years until a successful Moslem-Croat offensive last fall.
Fighting in Bosnia ended last October, when a country-wide ceasefire was declared. Bosnia's factions agreed a U.S.-sponsored peace accord in Dayton, Ohio, in November.
